prev: 7 Aug — Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. Turkey's parliament has not ratified it.

23–25 Sep — Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for an energy-only ceasefire and asked for a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump; Russia has not agreed. A 295-drone Russian barrage on Kyiv killed seven on the 25th.

24–25 Sep — Houthi missile and drone salvos on Riyadh and Saudi Aramco facilities; the three Mecca Pact military chiefs were summoned to urgent talks in Riyadh. Neither Pakistan nor Turkey has committed combat forces, and Washington has refused Saudi requests for US strikes on the Houthis.

25 Sep — Iran put its terms in public at the UN General Assembly: reopening Hormuz within seven days in exchange for released frozen funds, an end to sanctions and the lifting of the US naval blockade, conditional on restarting nuclear talks.
27 Sep — Trump rejected Iran's offer and would not rule out renewed strikes, closing off the one path that would have relieved oil quickly.

28–29 Sep — Brent peaked near $108 a barrel on the 28th, the highest since the Strait of Hormuz was shut in February, then fell to about $100 on the 29th as regional exports recovered to 12.8 million barrels a day in September (roughly 20 million before the war). Iran meanwhile claimed fresh attacks on shipping and US Navy vessels.
11–12 Oct — Trump announced an immediate Russia–Ukraine "energy ceasefire"; the Kremlin said talks were still ongoing and strikes on Ukrainian energy sites continued.

28 Oct — A local ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky was reported to be holding; Moscow and Kyiv were said to be awaiting US-led peace talks planned for next month. This is a one-city truce, not a general ceasefire.
today: The US carried out what it called defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz (reported 2–3 Nov), while Iran reportedly gave a two-day window for a Hormuz deal and the US side said talks were making progress. Headlines point both ways and Hormuz remains closed, so this is read as a continuation of the standoff rather than a new escalation.
Russia reportedly agreed to resume three-way talks with Kyiv and Washington (reported 21–22 Oct); the planned US-led talks are still pending.

2026-09-30.note: Brent near $100 a barrel is now only about 9% above where it sat a month ago, down from roughly 18-20% above at the $108 peak two days ago, and that compression is the whole of what reaches crypto from this. The route runs oil into headline inflation, headline inflation into the expected path of policy rates, and the rate path into the price of dollar liquidity — it is not a sentiment channel, and the dashboard does not treat it as one. Today you can watch the entire chain complete in a single number: the market-implied probability of an October Fed increase fell from 69.6% yesterday to 35.0% today, which lifted the L4 liquidity indicator out of negative territory and took the liquidity bucket from -100 to -70. The caution is that this is a repricing of expectations rather than of cash: the Treasury and the Fed's reverse repo facility are still draining dollars faster than at any point this month.
today: The oil war premium is unwinding in earnest. Brent settled near $100 a barrel on 29 September, down about 2.5% on the day and only around 9% above where it sat a month ago — against roughly 18–20% above a month ago when it peaked near $108 on the 28th. Bloomberg's 30 September market wrap has oil holding that loss, with Middle East exports now seen near pre-war levels. Supply is no longer arriving at a war price.

That fed straight through to the Fed, and it is the biggest single thing on the board today. New York Fed president John Williams said on 29 September that there is no urgency about another increase and no rush after September's hike, guiding towards just one more rise late in the year. The market-implied probability of an October increase fell from 69.6% to 35.0% in a day — the exact chain this section keeps describing, arriving in the one indicator that tracks it.

lead: The score rose from −15 ten sessions ago (28 Oct) to −7 today, and it was −18 at yesterday's refresh. Two indicators flipped up and one flipped down, and the two that flipped up are both marginal.
bullets: Price went from −10 to +17 because Bitcoin edged back above its 350-day average. Bitcoin ($75,891 on an unfinished Saturday) is 0.13% above its 350-day average (about $75,793) against a bullish line of at or above it, so that indicator turned bullish (lagging). It is 3.62% above its 200-day average (about $73,240, bullish, lagging) and 1.73% below its 100-day average (about $77,227, neutral, lagging). The 20-day high/low pattern and the share of the 5 largest altcoins above their 50-day average (none) stay bearish (coincident).

Liquidity rose from −30 to +3 on a single flip that is only just across its line. US government cash plus the Fed's reverse-repo balance is down $25.7bn over 20 days against a bullish line of down $25bn or more, so that indicator turned bullish (leading); a small move back the other way would undo it. The market-implied chance of a Fed rate increase at the 10 Dec meeting is 77.0% today, up from 67.0% yesterday and well above the 55% bearish line (leading, bearish). The dollar index is down 0.02 points over 20 days, inside its neutral band (leading, neutral).

Demand fell from −56 to −84 because Bitcoin ETF flows crossed their bearish line. Bitcoin ETF net flows over the last 20 trading days are −$1,051m against a bearish line of −$1,000m, up from a neutral −$978m yesterday, so that indicator turned bearish (coincident). Stablecoin supply is down 4.9% over 30 days against a −0.50% bearish line (leading, bearish), Ether ETF flows total −$1,246m over 20 trading days against a −$250m line (coincident, bearish), and the 7-day vs 28-day Bitcoin ETF flow trend is −$164m against a −$50m line (leading, bearish). Bitcoin 7-day volume is 0.972 times its 30-day average, neutral (coincident).

Positioning is unchanged at +53. Futures funding is +0.010% per 8 hours, inside the +0.005% to +0.030% bullish band (leading, bullish). Open interest is down 2.0% over 5 days while price fell, which scores neutral because leverage is being cleared out rather than added (leading, neutral).

Price and liquidity have both lifted off their lows, but on thin margins, while demand is deteriorating. The whole liquidity bucket is leading indicators and the whole price bucket is lagging ones, so when they disagree the composite understates whichever way liquidity points. Liquidity's +3 rests on a $0.7bn margin and the Fed-hike odds moved the wrong way, so it is not a clear signal. The composite is −7 and the regime is still Transition (no Bull or Bear streak in the last 15 sessions).

moves.t: if market odds of a Fed rate increase at the 10 Dec meeting fall below 55% (77.0% today; bullish below 30%). It slips back if US cash plus reverse repo stops falling by $25bn or more over 20 days (down $25.7bn today).

if stablecoin supply rises above −0.50% over 30 days (−4.9% today), or Ether ETF 20-day net flows improve to better than −$250m (−$1,246m today), or Bitcoin ETF 20-day net flows get back above −$1,000m (−$1,051m today). It stays weak while 7-day volume holds above 0.85 times its 30-day average (0.972 today).

a close below Bitcoin's 350-day average (about $75,793; $75,891 today, 0.13% above it) turns that indicator neutral again, and a close more than 3% below it (about $73,520) turns it bearish. The 200-day average (about $73,240) is the next support line.
if funding falls below +0.005% per 8 hours (+0.010% today), or if open interest rises 2%+ over 5 days while price falls (it is −2.0% over 5 days today), which would score bearish.
